chunks: With this chain, from al-Hasan, from Ismail ibn al-Zubayr, from 'Amr ibn Thabit, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever recites Surah Al-Ma'un in his obligatory and optional prayers will be among those whose prayers and fasting Allah, the Mighty and Sublime, has accepted, and he will not be called to account for what he did in the worldly life.

key_terms.سُورَةَ أَرَأَيْتَ: Surah Al-Ma'un (Chapter 107 of the Quran, named after its opening phrase 'Ara'ayta')

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting Surah Al-Ma'un in prayers?
ai.summary: Compiled by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Thawab al-A'mal*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) emphasizes the transformative power of reciting Surah Al-Ma'un specifically during obligatory and voluntary prayers. It promises not only the acceptance of worship but also a unique exemption from detailed accountability (*hisab*) for worldly deeds, highlighting the intercession of this Surah in mitigating divine judgment.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. From the previous chain from al-Hassan from Ismail b. al-Zubayr from ’Amru b. Thabit from Abi Ja’far (a.s.) who said:

Whoever recites Surah Maoon in his obligatory and optional prayers would be among those whose prayers and fasts are accepted by Allah, the Mighty and the Sublime, and that man would not be subjected to reckoning for whatever he has done in the world.
